Rule of thumb that held for magnitudes: an in-sample lab gain transfers at somewhere between 0 and ~1/6 of its size. It transfers at all only when the mechanism adds evidence the base lacked (a separate division network, better localisation). Mechanisms that trust more of the same in-sample model (edge filter, DivNet veto, ILP over relink) transferred at 0. To see +0.002 on the public LB we needed about +0.012 in the lab. Apart from the insertion, nothing on x138 came within 5x of that; the next best were the z shift (+0.0016) and leaf prune (+0.0008). Even perfect GT decisions on the tail reach only 1.19x the +0.012 bar, and 44b6 stays below it.

Three caveats on the ratio itself.
1. 1/6 comes from ONE mechanism read three times on ONE embryo at a 0.001 display step. Measured against the in-sample number, most of the "loss" may be in-sample inflation, not lab-to-LB loss: against the old-base OOF +0.0019 the ratio is not separable from 1. So it is an upper-bound guess for mechanisms that add evidence and ~0 for mechanisms that re-weight the same in-sample networks. Never apply it to oracle numbers.
2. Split every lab delta that changes the node set into a NODE term and an EVIDENCE term. A free 1% node drop is worth +0.0009 pooled (44b6 +0.0006), and its sign depends on the hidden embryo's N_pred/N_est (0.71 on 44b6 vs 1.02 on 6bba). Only the evidence term is expected to transfer. Round 13 found that most node-rule lab gains on x138 were the node term.
3. The ratio is a MAGNITUDE rule, not a sign rule. For re-thresholding a model inside a band where the lab has ~0 TP events (dc0.30: 0 TP / 6 FP removed on 6bba), even the sign does not transfer. Lab +0.0013 became public -0.005, roughly 2-4 public division TP events by the R15DS-1 model estimate. A lab arm with 0 TP events in the moved band bounds the TP loss only by the rule of three (<= ~3/N_TP), so it cannot sign a fork-removal knob.

## 2. Where the score was

- Detection and localisation. The gap to the top (0.975-0.978) is detection and localisation: 83% of missing GT nodes are absent upstream, and about half of FN edges are node misses (rounds 3 and 7). Miss anatomy on x138 (round 11, 668 missing GT nodes): 80% are multi-frame runs; most are not dim (72% vs 87% above threshold) but peakless (31% vs 70% have a raw max within 5 um), which points to crowding and merged peaks. Post-deadline detector work should target separation (I-113), not nnPU on dim cells.
- The tail ceiling, measured on x138 (exp60 ins35, 56 clips). The joint GT oracle of fork removal + orphan attach + links is +0.0143 (44b6 +0.0086, 6bba +0.0146). It is super-additive by +0.0015 through the division-Jaccard denominator (130 -> 99). Components: fork removal +0.0063; gated attach +0.0054; linking = the measured no-swap relink +0.0011 (the swap share, ~+0.006, is detection/localisation, not linking); wide attach +0.020 (joint +0.035); FP-edge removal +0.065, closed by LB evidence. The best realistic combination is +0.0004 in-sample and <= 0 out of sample (cross-embryo -0.0024, CV -0.0013). A learned classifier would need AUC ~0.94 on the wide pool and ~0.995 on the gated pool (binormal model, not measured). The metric has no unexploited lever for x138: the node-drop bonus pays only at P(annotated) < ~0.2%.
- Our models were frozen. The top teams retrained models. We froze ours on 25 Sep 13:38Z (R9) after our own retrains lost (0.920 all-199 scratch secondary, 0.937 fine-tuned secondary; our FT weights on public stacks are 0/4 on the LB).
- Divisions. The division term is 0.1 x div_J: 0.947 - 0.911 = 0.036 (P26, measured on exp29, not x138), so public J ~0.36. On the x138 lab J is 0.129 before the insertion and 0.192 with it (ins35 25/31/74). The break-even for an added fork is q* = J/(1+J) = 0.161, and for a removed fork the same p* = J/(1+J) on the shipped-stack bed. The only fork adder built on a separate division network (DaughterNet) transferred. Geometric orphan-attach adders measured -0.0129 (mirror-gated) / -0.0273 (nearest parent) on x138 (I-047), at precision 2.4-3.4% against a ~0.16 break-even.
  - Fork removers: dc0.30 (public -0.005), forkmid (T9/L3 lab FAIL), forkblob (FAIL on the pre-registered bed; +0.00019 on the ins35 bed, undecidable at n = 7), ANTIPAR, already-divided (probe 18) and DNVETO did not pay. The one exception was a sub-display public UP for fm45 on K2 (one dummy fork, not a final).
  - "Division knobs are invisible on public" was WRONG for DC-gated safe divisions above 0.25: that band is TP-rich on the public embryo (~0.0002-0.0003 display per dummy fork). As far as we know it still holds for insertion, cap and veto forks (probes 20, 35, 37/38).
  - x138's own safe-division knobs were first swept on x138 on 26 Sep (R13DP-1). In the lab, dc0.30 (6bba +0.0013) and divergence 2.5 were >= 0 on both embryos, symmetry tau was embryo-specific (6bba +0.005, 44b6 -0.001..-0.002), and three knobs never bind. The best both-embryo combination was +0.0018..0.0034 lab, 15-25% of the bar. The public then reversed the sign of the best-looking one (dc0.30).
- Sparse annotation. x138's readmitted and synthetic nodes match GT only ~1% of the time (73/13,284; 58/5,647). Matched shares differ by embryo: 44b6 0.79% vs 6bba 5.20% of predicted nodes. Most node-removal rules therefore act on unannotated cells, and the lab measures them with very low power.
- Node count (round 13, K2-like exp60 ins35 bed).
  - A FREE 1% node drop = +0.0009 pooled; a RANDOM 1% drop = -0.018..-0.021 (~21x; each matched node carries 1.85 TP edges).
  - The break-even enrichment r* = 0.03-0.05 is roughly density-free (enrichment ratio 0.6-1.9 across 20 arms, median ~1.1): public annotation density sets the noise, not the sign.
  - So the forum claim "the LB moves with the predicted node count" is just the metric's node factor. Pruning pays only if the pruned nodes are >= ~20x less likely to be real than an average node.
  - A node gate is necessary, not sufficient: the exp23 secondary swap was +0.62% nodes vs its base and lost 0.007 on the LB, of which node count predicts only ~-0.0006.
- Where the 0.955+ teams were (intel 26 Sep 20:30-22:46Z; reach0955/r_intel.json, intel_0960_0966.json, discussions_2026-09-26.json).
  - 136 teams at 0.955-0.959 and 53 at 0.960-0.966 (47 of their 81 members have no public kernel or dataset). Nobody in either band published the code or weights behind the score; the Code and Models tabs still topped out at 0.953 at the last check (27 Sep 08:32Z; [F4]).

## 3. Process lessons

1. Reproduce first. Spend one probe on a verbatim copy before building on a public notebook (x138 reproduced exactly; takaito lost 0.007).
2. Pre-register before the score. The READ TABLE (written 25 Sep 23:12Z, clarified in v2-v4, all before #37/#38 scored) made the 26 Sep 07:35Z finals read mechanical: row 3, no OK needed. Rules written after a number (ADDENDUM M, round 2) were labelled post-hoc and changed nothing.
   - The same held for the ladder. L9 was logged at 20:49Z before the first rung, and L5v2 plus the attribution protocol (R13-A1) at 01:31Z before any rung scored. D1 and D2 were then read mechanically (no BASE, no combo, pair unchanged).
   - Pre-approval also bought speed. K2 went in at 26 Sep ~00:02Z and sat 12th-16th of ~100 in the 0.954 block (ties go to the earlier submission), ~85 places above where a late copy lands.
3. Kill tests and power clauses stopped ideas that looked cheap (head retrain, forkmid, forkblob, ANTIPAR, K3b). Not one closed idea had shown an LB gain through 26 Sep. After the user lifted the knob-ladder clause (20:33Z), lp30, dc0.30 and fm45 were reopened as public rungs only (probes 39-42):
   - lp30 was NEU;
   - dc0.30 was -0.005 with the lab sign wrong;
   - fm45 showed an attributable sub-display UP, which is the one counterexample and is below the display step.
   The closures cost no visible score. The dc0.30 read also shows what an un-gated "lab-positive" knob can do.
4. Sha-identity dummies made every "off" path provably byte-identical (K1 dummy == exp57b; FF CSV == exp56; twin = K2 minus 12 fork edges; every ladder file = K2 plus its knob override: a cell-0 line for the DC and forkmid rungs, plus the prune call for lp30). Fail-soft stages (safetail) made the runtime risk measurable. The declared exception: the secswap stage fails loudly on purpose.
5. Runtime is a first-class risk.
   - Our only runtime evidence is latency from our own 10-min poller: L = (last PENDING poll, first COMPLETE poll], widened when a CLI call failed.
   - Paired submissions ran concurrently, so the twin doubled as a runtime control: the insertion costs <= L(K2)_hi - L(twin)_lo = 0.85 h on the hidden run. Hidden reruns did not count against our GPU quota.
   - Latencies against the 12 h limit: x138 <= 6.46 h, x138 + insertion (6.72, 7.73], K2 (7.36, 7.54], twin (6.69, 6.87], ladder exp70a (6.87, 7.04], exp70d (7.19, 7.36], exp70e (7.24, 7.42], exp70b (7.41, 7.58] h. In every ladder file the per-clip 8.0 h insertion gate did NOT fire. No finals-relevant file errored or timed out.
   - The #35 latency bound stayed too wide to prove it clean because of the 15:26-16:06Z empty-CLI gap; that one gap now confounds C1 and C4 (R12P-1).
   - Several agents on one account hit HTTP 429 on kernels output and ListSubmissions (26 Sep 20:34-20:47Z; one 21.6 min gap between good polls). The fix: around score times, one API caller only (the 04:10-06:45Z quiet window), 60 s backoff, and a missing file is never read as a content failure. The ladder watcher then made 64 calls with 0 x 429.
6. LB mechanics.
   - Scores show 3 decimals, so the ~350-380 teams at 0.953 are ordered by unrounded score, and ties go to the earlier submission. Late copies land at the bottom of their block (every observed x138-copy window did: 15 by 27 Sep 05:32Z).
   - Our public rank drifted from #155 to #255 at the same 0.954 (26-27 Sep) while the field grew; that is not a signal.
   - Our LB row's SubmissionCount and LastSubmissionDate count only SCORED submissions (round 13). An in-block move is therefore attributable to a probe only when the count rises by exactly one between two fresh downloads; the UP test "a team ranked above us is now below us" works because public bests never decrease. This protocol turned exp70b's display-invisible 0.954 into a readable UP (6 TeamIds passed) and kept exp70a's 0.954 honestly NEU.
7. Compute the ceiling before the search.
   - After the 25 Sep freeze, rounds 2-[F6] of wf_ideas_v4 (~15-24 agents each) plus one combo-oracle measurement produced rule clarifications, closures and one stopped candidate (overlap consensus: G-A 43/62 < 60), but no score from a new mechanism. The E10 successor watch fired no port trigger [F4].
   - The combo oracle (26 Sep 19:13Z) showed that perfect GT decisions on forks, orphans and links give +0.0143 lab, 1.19x the +0.012 bar (realistic +0.0004 in-sample, <= 0 out of sample). Run on 25 Sep, it would have ended the inference-only search ~10 rounds earlier.
   - Rule: measure a family's GT-oracle ceiling first; below 2x the bar, fund at most one round.
8. Check the rules text before setting policy. Two things we treated as "not allowed" (overlap consensus, an in-kernel sweep) were our own caution. The only TEST-DATA prohibition is hand labelling (3.4.b); private sharing of code or data is banned (3.5.d, 3.6.a), and original work (3.14.a) and no unfair practices (3.8.d) also bind. Check the rules early, then decide on method grounds. Name our own rules by content, not by number: the 26 Sep 20:30-20:49Z entries called the lifted knob-ladder clause "R7", although PRE-REGISTRATION v3 lists it under R9 (R12-A3 (a)).
9. Leaked material (cached private CSVs in public datasets) is neither usable nor allowed. A static CSV cannot score in a code-competition rerun, and the rules require original work (3.14.a, 3.8.d).
10. "Keep more/shorter components" rules win in the lab through node count and do not transfer: round-3 boundary rescue, MIN_TRACK_LEN L4 (probe 6 = -0.002), I-146 on x138 (round 10: +0.00033, W/L 7/47, carried by 3 tiny clips).
11. Pre-registration versus competitiveness. Items (a)-(g) and the do-differently list were written 27 Sep ~02:00Z, BEFORE any ladder or private score; (f') was added after the ladder read. Do not rewrite after the private LB; add a dated post-private note in section 7 instead.
    - WHAT THE RULES PROTECTED AGAINST:
      - (a) choosing finals on 0.001 public differences measured on one embryo while 71% of the score sits on other embryos (the READ TABLE made the 26 Sep 07:35Z finals read mechanical);
      - (b) in-sample lab gains that do not transfer: the edge filter (+0.016 lab, 0/-0.001 LB), fork removers, overlap consensus (stopped by its own G-A, later confirmed -0.00143), head retrain (killed by the embryo-held-out test, +12% worse);
      - (c) runtime and engineering failure near the deadline (safetail, byte-identical-when-off, sha dummies; no finals file errored or timed out);
      - (d) post-hoc self-deception (ADDENDUM M labelled post-hoc and ignored).

The rounding makes the true step anything in (0, ~0.002), so the ratio is (0, 1/3) against the in-sample +0.0058..0.0065, but (0, ~1) against the only OOF number (+0.0019, old exp39 base, precision 4/15). The lab bar '>= 6x the target' is therefore an IN-SAMPLE-to-LB bar. Transfer from an honest OOF lab may be much better than 1/6. Mechanism: in-sample inflation of the insertion (DaughterNet selected and thresholded on the same clips). Testable: (a) PRIVATE-READ v2 (e) already reports r as an interval, so it just needs the OOF denominator shown alongside; (b) post-deadline s4 item 8 gives the first x138 OOF insertion number. If x138 OOF >= +0.004 while the public stays +0.001, the '1/6 lab-to-LB' reading survives; if OOF ~+0.001-0.002, the post-deadline bar for OOF-measured items drops to ~2-3x.
